title.zh: 卷六十一 唐書37: 列傳13 安金全 安元信 安重霸 劉訓 張敬詢 劉彥琮 袁建豐 西方鄴 張遵誨 孫璋
title.en: Volume 61 Book of Later Tang 37: Biographies 13 - An Jingquan, An Yuanxin, An Zhongba, Liu Xun, Zhang Jingxun, Liu Yancong, Yuan Jianfeng, Xi Fangye, Zhang Zunhui, Sun Zhang
title.raw: 卷六十一 唐書37: 列傳13 安金全 安元信 安重霸 劉訓 張敬詢 劉彥琮 袁建豐 西方鄴 張遵誨 孫璋 Volume 61 Book of Later Tang 37: Biographies 13 - An Jingquan, An Yuanxin, An Zhongba, Liu Xun, Zhang Jingxun, Liu Yancong, Yuan Jianfeng, Xi Fangye, Zhang Zunhui, Sun Zhang

sentences.zh: 安金全，代北人。

translations.literal: An Jinquan was a man of northern Dai.
translations.idiomatic: An Jinquan came from northern Dai.

sentences.zh: 世為邊將，少驍果，便騎射。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been frontier generals; in youth he was valiant and resolute, skilled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served for generations as frontier commanders; from youth he was bold and adept at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 武皇時為騎將，屢從征討。

translations.literal: In the Martial Emperor's time he served as a cavalry officer and repeatedly followed campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Martial Emperor he served as a cavalry commander and took part in many campaigns.

sentences.zh: 莊宗之救潞州及平河朔，皆有戰功，累為刺史，以老病退居太原。

translations.literal: In Emperor Zhuangzong's relief of Luzhou and pacification of Heshuo he had merit in battle; he was repeatedly made prefect and, owing to age and illness, retired to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself when Emperor Zhuangzong relieved Luzhou and pacified Heshuo, rose through several prefectural posts, and finally retired to Taiyuan because of age and infirmity.

sentences.zh: 天祐中，汴將王檀率師三萬，乘莊宗在鄴，來襲并州。

translations.literal: In the Tianyou era the Bian general Wang Tan led thirty thousand troops and, taking advantage of Emperor Zhuangzong's being at Ye, came to attack Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianyou reign the Liang general Wang Tan marched thirty thousand men against Bingzhou while Emperor Zhuangzong was away at Ye.

sentences.zh: 時城無備兵，敵軍奄至，監軍張承業大恐，計無所出，閱諸司丁匠，登陴禦捍。

translations.literal: At the time the city had no ready troops; the enemy army arrived suddenly. Army Supervisor Zhang Chengye was greatly alarmed and could think of no plan, so he reviewed the laborers and artisans of the various offices and had them mount the walls to defend.
translations.idiomatic: The city had no garrison on hand when the enemy appeared without warning. Army Supervisor Zhang Chengye was terrified and at a loss until he mustered artisans and laborers from the government workshops to man the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 外攻甚急，金全遽出謂承業曰：「老夫退居抱病，不任軍事。

translations.literal: The outside assault was very pressing. Jinquan hurried out and said to Chengye: "This old man has retired and is ill; I am not fit for military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As the assault grew fierce, Jinquan came forward at once and told Chengye, "I have retired and am ill; I am in no condition to command.

sentences.zh: 然吾王家屬在此，王業本根之地，如一旦為敵所有，大事去矣。

translations.literal: Yet the royal clan is here, and this is the rootland of the imperial enterprise. If it should in a single day fall to the enemy, the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: But the royal household is here—this is the foundation of the throne. If the enemy takes it in a day, everything is lost.

sentences.zh: 請以庫甲見授，為公備寇。

translations.literal: Please grant me the armory armor; I will prepare against the invaders for you.
translations.idiomatic: Give me what armor the storehouses hold, and I will help you repel them.

sentences.zh: 」承業即時授之。

translations.literal: " Chengye at once handed them over.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengye handed over the arms immediately.

sentences.zh: 金全被甲跨馬，召率子弟及退閑諸將，得數百人。

translations.literal: Jinquan donned armor, mounted a horse, summoned and led his sons and younger kin together with retired and idle generals, and gathered several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: He armored himself, mounted, and rallied his sons and kinsmen along with retired officers until he had several hundred men.

sentences.zh: 夜出北門，擊賊於羊馬城內，梁人驚潰，由是退卻。

translations.literal: At night he went out the north gate and struck the bandits within the sheep-and-horse enclosure; the Liang men were startled and routed, and thereby withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That night he sallied from the north gate and struck the enemy in the livestock pens outside the wall; the Liang troops broke in panic and drew off.

sentences.zh: 俄而石君立自潞州至，汴軍退走。

translations.literal: Before long Shi Junli arrived from Luzhou and the Bian army retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shi Junli came up from Luzhou, and the Liang army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 微金全之奮命，城幾危矣。

translations.literal: But for Jinquan's staking his life, the city would nearly have been lost.
translations.idiomatic: Without Jinquan's desperate stand, the city would almost certainly have fallen.

sentences.zh: 莊宗性矜伐，凡大將立功，不時行賞，故金全終莊宗世，名位不進。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong was by nature proud and boastful; whenever great generals achieved merit he did not reward them promptly, so Jinquan through Emperor Zhuangzong's entire reign did not advance in fame or rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangzong was vain and slow to reward victorious commanders, and Jinquan therefore gained no further promotion throughout Zhuangzong's reign.

sentences.zh: 明宗與之有舊，及登極，授金全同平章事，充振武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong had old ties with him; when he ascended the throne he appointed Jinquan Associate Grand Councillor and made him military commissioner of the Zhenwu army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong had known him long before; on taking the throne he made Jinquan Associate Grand Councillor and commissioner of the Zhenwu circuit.

sentences.zh: 在任二年，治民為政非所長，詔赴闕，俄而病卒。

translations.literal: After two years in office, governing the people and administering affairs were not his strengths; he was ordered to the capital and soon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in the post—civil administration was never his strength—he was recalled to court and died of illness shortly after.

sentences.zh: 廢視朝二日。

translations.literal: Court audiences were suspended for two days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court audiences for two days.

sentences.zh: 初，南北對壘，汴之遊騎每出，必為金全所獲，故梁之偵邏者鹹懼，目之為「安五道」，蓋比鬼將有五道之名也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when north and south faced each other in camp, whenever Bian raiding cavalry went out they were invariably captured by Jinquan, so Liang scouts all feared him and called him "An of the Five Roads," likening him to the demon general who bears the name of the Five Roads.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the two sides faced each other along the front, Liang raiders sent out were almost always taken by Jinquan; Liang scouts dreaded him and nicknamed him "An of the Five Roads," after a demon general of that name.

sentences.zh: 子審琦等，皆位至方鎮，別有傳。

translations.literal: His sons Shenqi and others all rose to military commissioner posts; they have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shenqi and the rest all rose to governorships of frontier circuits and are treated in separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 審通，金全之猶子也。

translations.literal: Shentong was Jinquan's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong was a nephew of Jinquan.

sentences.zh: 幼事莊宗，累有戰功，轉先鋒指揮使。

translations.literal: From youth he served Emperor Zhuangzong, repeatedly had merit in battle, and was transferred to vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Zhuangzong's service as a youth, won repeated distinction in battle, and was promoted to commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 同光初，為北京右廂馬軍都指揮使，屯奉化軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was commander of the right wing of the Northern Capital horse army and was stationed at the Fenghua army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongguang era he commanded the right wing of the Northern Capital cavalry and was posted to the Fenghua garrison.

sentences.zh: 四年春，赴明宗急詔，軍趨夷臒，為前鋒。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he answered Emperor Mingzong's urgent summons; the army hastened to Yimen and he served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year he answered Mingzong's urgent summons, marched the army toward Yimen, and led the van.

sentences.zh: 天成初，授單州刺史，改齊州防禦使，兼諸道先鋒馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was made prefect of Shanzhou, then changed to defense commissioner of Qizhou, and concurrently commander of the vanguard horse armies of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiancheng reign he was made prefect of Shan, then defense commissioner of Qi, while retaining command of the vanguard cavalry of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 奉詔北征，從房知溫營於盧台。

translations.literal: He received orders for the northern campaign and followed Fang Zhiwen's encampment at Lutai.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered north on campaign, he joined Fang Zhiwen's camp at Lutai.

sentences.zh: 會龍至部下兵亂，審通脫身酒筵，奪般以濟，促騎士介馬，及亂兵南行，盡戮之，以功授檢校太傅、滄州節度使。

translations.literal: When the Longzhi subordinates mutinied, Shentong escaped from the wine feast, seized a boat to cross, urged the horsemen to saddle, overtook the mutineers marching south, and slaughtered them all; for this merit he was appointed acting Grand Mentor and military commissioner of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Longzhi's troops mutinied, Shentong left the banquet, commandeered a boat to cross the water, armed his riders, overtook the rebels marching south, and killed them to a man; for this he was made acting Grand Mentor and commissioner of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 圍王都於中山，躬冒矢石，為飛石所中而卒。

translations.literal: Besieging Wang Du at Zhongshan, he personally braved arrows and stones, was struck by a flying stone, and died.
translations.idiomatic: While besieging Wang Du at Zhongshan he exposed himself to missile fire and was killed by a stone cast from the wall.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 安元信，字子言，代北人。

translations.literal: An Yuanxin, style Ziyan, was a man of northern Dai.
translations.idiomatic: An Yuanxin, whose style was Ziyan, came from northern Dai.

sentences.zh: 父順琳，為降野軍使。

translations.literal: His father Shunlin was commissioner of the Jiangye army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shunlin served as commander of the Jiangye garrison.

sentences.zh: 元信以將族子，便騎射，幼事武皇，從平巢、蔡。

translations.literal: Yuanxin, as a son of a general's clan, was skilled at riding and shooting; in youth he served the Martial Emperor and followed the pacification of Huang Chao and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Born into a military family, he was adept at horsemanship and archery and entered the Martial Emperor's service young, fighting through the campaigns against Huang Chao and Qin Zongquan.

sentences.zh: 光啟中，吐渾赫連鐸寇雲中，武皇使元信拒之，元信兵敗於居庸關。

translations.literal: In the Guangqi era the Tujue Helian Duo raided Yunzhong; the Martial Emperor sent Yuanxin to resist him, and Yuanxin's army was defeated at Juyong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangqi the Tujue chieftain Helian Duo raided Yunzhong; the Martial Emperor sent Yuanxin against him, and Yuanxin was defeated at Juyong Pass.

sentences.zh: 武皇性嚴急，元信不敢還，遂奔定州；

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor was stern and harsh by nature; Yuanxin dared not return and therefore fled to Dingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Emperor was severe; Yuanxin did not dare go back and fled to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 王處存待之甚厚，用為突騎都校。

translations.literal: Wang Chucun treated him very generously and employed him as commander of the shock cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun received him warmly and made him commander of the shock cavalry.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，處存子郜嗣位。

translations.literal: In the Qianning era Chucun's son Gao succeeded to the post.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianning, Chucun's son Gao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 時梁軍攻河朔三鎮，奔命不暇，梁將張存敬軍奄至城下，既無宿備，郜懼，挈其族奔太原，元信從之；

translations.literal: At the time the Liang army attacked the three Hebei circuits and they had no respite from urgent calls; the Liang general Zhang Cunjing's army suddenly reached the walls. With no prior preparations, Gao was afraid, took his clan and fled to Taiyuan, and Yuanxin followed;
translations.idiomatic: The Liang were pressing the three Hebei circuits and Gao had no time to prepare when Zhang Cunjing's army appeared before the walls. In fear Gao took his family to Taiyuan, and Yuanxin went with him.

sentences.zh: 武皇待之如初，用為鐵林軍使。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor treated him as before and employed him as commander of the Iron Forest army.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Emperor welcomed him as before and appointed him commander of the Iron Forest guard.

sentences.zh: 梁將氏叔琮之攻河東也，別將葛從周自馬嶺入，元信伏於榆次，挫其前鋒。

translations.literal: When the Liang general Shi Shuzong attacked Hedong, the separate commander Ge Congzhou entered by Maling; Yuanxin lay in ambush at Yuci and checked his vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Shuzong attacked Hedong and Ge Congzhou came in by Maling, Yuanxin ambushed him at Yuci and broke his leading columns.

sentences.zh: 梁將李思安之攻上黨也，王師將壁高河，為梁軍所逼。

translations.literal: When the Liang general Li Si'an attacked Shangdang, the royal army was about to entrench at Gaohe but was pressed by the Liang army.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Si'an of Liang attacked Shangdang, the Jin army was trying to hold Gaohe but was hard pressed by Liang forces.

sentences.zh: 別將秦武者，尤為難敵，元信與鬥，斃之。

translations.literal: The separate commander Qin Wu was especially hard to oppose; Yuanxin fought him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Their subordinate Qin Wu was a formidable opponent; Yuanxin met him in combat and killed him.

sentences.zh: 由是梁軍解去，城壘得立。

translations.literal: Thereby the Liang army dispersed and left, and the walls and ramparts were secured.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang army then withdrew, and the defenses held.

sentences.zh: 武皇賜所乘馬及細鎧仗，遷突陣都將。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor bestowed the horse he himself rode and fine armor and weapons, and promoted him to commander of the assault formation.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Emperor gave him his own mount, fine armor, and arms, and promoted him to commander of the assault corps.

sentences.zh: 莊宗嗣晉王位，元信從救上黨，破夾寨，復澤、潞，以功授檢校司空、遼州刺史，賜玉鞭名馬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong succeeded to the Jin throne, Yuanxin followed the relief of Shangdang, broke the encircling camps, and recovered Ze and Lu; for merit he was appointed acting Minister of Works and prefect of Liaozhou, and was given a jade whip and a famous horse.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong succeeded to the Jin throne, Yuanxin joined the relief of Shangdang, broke the encircling camps, and recovered Ze and Lu; he was made acting Minister of Works and prefect of Liao, and received a jade whip and a celebrated horse.

sentences.zh: 柏鄉之役，日晚戰酣，元信重傷，莊宗自臨傅藥。

translations.literal: At the battle of Baixiang, as evening came the fighting grew fierce; Yuanxin was gravely wounded, and Emperor Zhuangzong personally came to apply medicine.
translations.idiomatic: At Baixiang, as dusk fell and the fighting raged, Yuanxin was badly wounded; Zhuangzong came in person to dress his wounds.

sentences.zh: 其年，改檢校司徒、武州刺史，充內衙副都指揮使、山北諸州都團練副使。

translations.literal: That year he was changed to acting Minister of Education and prefect of Wuzhou, and served as deputy commander of the inner palace guard and deputy overseer of training for all circuits north of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was made acting Minister of Education and prefect of Wu, with the posts of deputy commander of the inner guard and deputy overseer of the northern circuits.

sentences.zh: 從莊宗定魏博，移為博州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Zhuangzong in pacifying Weibo and was transferred to be prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhuangzong in pacifying Weibo and was transferred to prefect of Bo.

sentences.zh: 與梁對壘德勝渡，元信為右廂排陣使。

translations.literal: Facing Liang across Desheng Ford, Yuanxin was right-wing battle-array officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies faced each other at Desheng Ford, Yuanxin commanded the right wing in battle order.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為大同軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he became military commissioner of the Datong army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made commissioner of the Datong circuit.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平定河南，移授橫海軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Henan, he was transferred and appointed military commissioner of the Henghai army.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong pacified Henan, Yuanxin was transferred to commissioner of the Henghai circuit.

sentences.zh: 時契丹犯邊，元信與霍彥威從明宗屯常山。

translations.literal: At the time the Khitan raided the frontier; Yuanxin and Huo Yanwei followed Emperor Mingzong in encamping at Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided the border, Yuanxin and Huo Yanwei campaigned with Mingzong at Changshan.

sentences.zh: 元信恃功，每對明宗以成敗勇怯戲侮彥威，彥威不敢答。

translations.literal: Yuanxin relied on his merit and, in Emperor Mingzong's presence, would mock Yanwei with talk of victory and defeat, courage and cowardice; Yanwei dared not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxin, proud of his record, would bait Yanwei before Mingzong with jibes about who had won or lost and who was brave or timid; Yanwei never answered back.

sentences.zh: 明宗曰：「成由天地，不由於人。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong said: "Success lies with Heaven and Earth, not with men.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said, "Victory belongs to Heaven and earth, not to any man.

sentences.zh: 當氏叔琮圍太原，公有何勇！

translations.literal: When Shi Shuzong besieged Taiyuan, what courage did you have!
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Shuzong besieged Taiyuan, what courage did you show then!

sentences.zh: 今國家運興，致我等富貴。

translations.literal: Now the state's fortune rises and has brought us wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: It is the dynasty's rising fortune that has made us rich and honored.

sentences.zh: 」勿以小勝小捷掛於口吻，取笑於長者。

translations.literal: " Do not hang small victories and small successes on your lips and make sport of your elders.
translations.idiomatic: " Do not parade petty triumphs in your speech and make a laughingstock of yourself before your seniors.

sentences.zh: 元信乃起謝，不復以彥威為戲。

translations.literal: Yuanxin then rose and apologized and no longer made sport of Yanwei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxin rose to apologize and never again mocked Yanwei.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，以元信嘗為內衙都校，尤厚待之，加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, because Yuanxin had once been chief of the inner palace guard he treated him with special favor and added the title Associate Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong came to the throne he treated Yuanxin with exceptional favor because they had served together in the inner guard, and made him Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 明年，移鎮徐州。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to garrison Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 王師之討高季興，襄帥劉訓逗撓軍期，移授元信山南東道節度使以代訓。

translations.literal: When the royal army attacked Gao Jixing, the Xiang military commissioner Liu Xun dallied and delayed the campaign schedule; Yuanxin was transferred and appointed military commissioner of the Shannan East circuit to replace Xun.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Gao Jixing, the Xiang commander Liu Xun dragged his feet; Yuanxin was made commissioner of Shannan East to replace him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，改歸德軍節度使，就加兼侍中。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was changed to military commissioner of the Guide army and was at the same time additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to commissioner of Guide and concurrently made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 明宗不豫，求入。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong fell ill, he requested to enter the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong fell ill, he asked to return to court.

sentences.zh: 末帝即位，授潞州節度使，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, he was appointed military commissioner of Luzhou and added acting Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor succeeded, Yuanxin was made commissioner of Lu and acting Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 清泰三年二月，以疾卒於鎮，時年七十四。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Qingtai he died of illness in his commission; he was then seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Qingtai 3 he died of illness at his post, aged seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 贈太師。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖即位，以元信宿望，令禮官定諡曰忠懿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Jin took the throne, because of Yuanxin's long-standing repute he ordered the ritual officers to fix his posthumous title as Loyal and Admirable.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin founder Gaozu came to the throne, he honored Yuanxin's long service by having the ritual officers confer the posthumous name Loyal and Admirable.

sentences.zh: 有子六人，長曰友權，曆諸衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He had six sons; the eldest was Youquan, who served in turn as great general of the various guards.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons. The eldest, Youquan, rose through the great generalships of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 次曰友親，為滁州刺史，卒於任。

translations.literal: The next was Youqin, who was prefect of Chuzhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The second, Youqin, served as prefect of Chu and died in office.

sentences.zh: 安重霸，雲州人也。

translations.literal: An Zhongba was a man of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An Zhongba came from Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 性狡譎，多智算。

translations.literal: By nature he was crafty and cunning, with much stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He was cunning and full of schemes.

sentences.zh: 初，自代北與明宗俱事武皇，因負罪奔梁；

translations.literal: At first, from northern Dai he and Emperor Mingzong together served the Martial Emperor; because of a crime he fled to Liang;
translations.idiomatic: He had served the Martial Emperor in northern Dai alongside Mingzong, then fled to Liang after a crime.

sentences.zh: 在梁復以罪奔蜀，蜀以蕃人善騎射，因為親將。

translations.literal: In Liang he again fled to Shu because of a crime; Shu, because he was a frontier man skilled at riding and shooting, made him a personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: He fled Liang for Shu on another charge; Shu valued his frontier horsemanship and made him a personal guard.

sentences.zh: 蜀後主王衍，幼年襲位，其政多僻。

translations.literal: The Later Lord of Shu, Wang Yan, succeeded to the throne in his youth; his government was largely perverse.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's young ruler Wang Yan came to the throne as a boy, and his rule was deeply erratic.

sentences.zh: 宦官王承休居中用事，與成都尹韓昭內外相結，專采擇聲色，以固寵幸。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Chengxu held power at court and, with the Chengdu prefect Han Zhao linking inside and outside, devoted themselves solely to gathering music and beauty to secure favor.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Chengxu dominated the court, conspiring with the Chengdu prefect Han Zhao to stock the palace with entertainers and secure their hold on the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 武臣宿將，居常切齒。

translations.literal: Martial officials and veteran generals constantly gnashed their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: The old military commanders ground their teeth in rage.

sentences.zh: 重霸諂事承休，特見委信。

translations.literal: Zhongba flattered and served Chengxu and was especially entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongba curried favor with Chengxu and won his special trust.

sentences.zh: 梁末，岐下削弱，蜀人奪取秦、成、階等州，重霸說承休求鎮秦州。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang, Qi territory was weakened and the Shu seized Qin, Cheng, Jie, and other prefectures; Zhongba persuaded Chengxu to request garrison of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Liang, as Qi weakened, Shu seized Qin, Cheng, Jie, and neighboring prefectures; Zhongba urged Chengxu to seek the Qinzhou commission.

sentences.zh: 仍於軍中選山東驍果，得數千人，號龍武都，以承休為軍帥，重霸副焉，俱在天水。

translations.literal: He also selected from the army fierce fighters from Shandong, obtaining several thousand men, styled the Dragon Martial Division; Chengxu was made army commander and Zhongba his deputy, both at Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: From the army he picked several thousand fierce fighters from the east, called them the Dragon Martial Division, made Chengxu their commander with Zhongba as deputy, and stationed them at Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，承休欲求旄鉞，乃以隴西花木入獻，又稱秦州山水之美，人物之盛，請後主臨幸，而韓昭讚成之。

translations.literal: After more than a year Chengxu wished to obtain the commander's baton and axe; he therefore presented flowers and trees of Longxi as tribute, and again praised the beauty of Qinzhou's mountains and waters and the abundance of its people, requesting that the Later Lord visit in person, while Han Zhao urged it on.
translations.idiomatic: After a year Chengxu wanted a full military commission; he sent Longxi flowers and trees as tribute, praised Qinzhou's scenery and beauties, and asked the emperor to visit in person, with Han Zhao seconding the plan.

sentences.zh: （《太平廣記》引《王氏見聞錄》云：承休請從諸軍揀選官健，得驍勇數千，號龍武軍，承休自為統帥，並特加衣糧，日有優給。

translations.literal: (The 《Taiping Guangji》 cites the 《Wangshi Jianwenlu》 as saying: Chengxu requested to pick out officers and soldiers from the various armies and obtained several thousand fierce warriors, styled the Dragon Martial army; Chengxu himself was commander, and they were all given extra clothing and grain with daily preferential allowances.)
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Taiping Guangji》, citing the 《Wangshi Jianwenlu》: Chengxu asked to select troops from every army and gathered several thousand elite fighters called the Dragon Martial army under his own command, with extra rations and daily allowances.)

sentences.zh: 因乞秦州節度使，且云：「願與陛下於秦州采掇美麗。

translations.literal: He therefore begged for military commissioner of Qinzhou and said: "I wish together with Your Majesty to gather beauties at Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked for the Qinzhou commission, saying, "I wish to gather beauties at Qinzhou together with Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」且說秦州風土，多出國色，仍請幸天水。

translations.literal: " He also said that Qinzhou's customs produce many beauties of the realm, and again requested that the emperor visit Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: " He added that Qinzhou's countrywomen were famed for their beauty and again asked the emperor to visit Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 少主甚悅，即遣仗節赴鎮，應所選龍武精銳，並充衙隊從行。）〉

translations.literal: The young lord was greatly pleased, immediately sent credentials to take up the commission, and all the selected Dragon Martial elite served as his escort guard on the journey.) 〉
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor was delighted, sent him off with credentials to his post, and made the Dragon Martial elite his escort on the march.)]

sentences.zh: 同光二年十月，蜀主率眾數萬，由劍閣將出興、鳳，以遊秦州；

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Tongguang the Shu ruler led several tens of thousands of men, by Jian'ge intending to go out toward Xing and Feng to tour Qinzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Tongguang 2 the Shu emperor led tens of thousands through Jian'ge toward Xing and Feng on his way to tour Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 至興州，遇魏王繼岌軍至，狼狽而旋。

translations.literal: Reaching Xingzhou, he encountered the army of Prince of Wei Jiji arriving and turned back in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingzhou he met the army of Prince Jiji of Wei and fled back in disorder.

sentences.zh: 承休遽聞東師入討，大恐，計無從出，問於重霸。

translations.literal: Chengxiu suddenly heard that the eastern army had entered to attack; he was greatly afraid and could think of no plan, and asked Zhongba.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu heard abruptly that the eastern armies were advancing, was terrified, and asked Zhongba what to do.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「開府何患？

translations.literal: He replied: "What does the Commissioner worry about?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongba answered, "What is there to fear, Commissioner?

sentences.zh: 蜀中精兵，不下十萬，咫尺之險，安有不濟，縱東軍盡如狼虎，豈能入劍門！

translations.literal: Shu's crack troops are no fewer than a hundred thousand; with peril a foot away, how could they not succeed? Even if the eastern army were all wolves and tigers, how could they enter Jianmen!
translations.idiomatic: Shu has a hundred thousand elite troops, and the passes are at hand—how can we fail? Even if every eastern soldier were a wolf or tiger, they cannot pass Jianmen!

sentences.zh: 然國家有患，開府特受主知，不得失於奔赴，此州製置事定，無虞得失，重霸願從開府赴闕。

translations.literal: Yet the state has trouble; the Commissioner is especially known to the ruler and must not fail to hurry to his aid. Once this prefecture's arrangements are settled there is no worry over gain or loss; Zhongba wishes to follow the Commissioner to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: But the realm is in peril and you enjoy the emperor's special trust—you must not fail to go to him. Once affairs here are settled there is nothing to lose; Zhongba will accompany you to court.

sentences.zh: 」承休素信以為忠赤。

translations.literal: " Chengxu had long trusted him and took this as loyal sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengxu, who had always trusted him, took this for loyal devotion.

sentences.zh: 重霸出秦州金帛以賂群羌，買由州山路歸蜀。

translations.literal: Zhongba took Qinzhou gold and silks to bribe the various Qiang and bought a mountain road through Youzhou to return to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongba spent Qinzhou gold and silk bribing the Qiang tribes to open a mountain route back into Shu through Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 承休擁龍武軍及招置僅萬人從行，令重霸權握部署，州人祖送，秦州軍亦列部隊。

translations.literal: Chengxiu led the Dragon Martial army and those he had recruited, nearly ten thousand men on the march; he had Zhongba hold temporary authority over deployment. The people of the prefecture saw him off, and the Qinzhou army also formed ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu marched with the Dragon Martial division and recruits, nearly ten thousand men, leaving Zhongba in charge of arrangements; the prefectural populace and Qinzhou troops turned out to see them off.

sentences.zh: 承休登乘，重霸馬前辭曰：「國家費盡事力，收獲隴西，若從開府南行，隴州即時疏失，請開府自行，重霸且為國守藩。

translations.literal: As Chengxu mounted, Zhongba took leave before his horse and said: "The state exhausted its strength to recover Longxi. If you follow the Commissioner south, Longzhou would at once be left undefended. Please go on alone, Commissioner; Zhongba will for the time being guard the frontier for the state.
translations.idiomatic: As Chengxu mounted his horse, Zhongba bowed from the stirrup and said, "The state spent everything to win Longxi. If you march south, Longzhou will be left empty at once. Go on alone, Commissioner—I will hold the frontier for the realm.

sentences.zh: 」 承休既去，重霸在秦州，聞明宗起河北，即時遣使以秦、成等州來降。

translations.literal: " After Chengxu had gone, Zhongba was at Qinzhou; hearing that Emperor Mingzong had risen in Hebei, he at once sent envoys to surrender Qin, Cheng, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: " Once Chengxu had departed, Zhongba heard that Mingzong had risen in Hebei and immediately sent envoys offering Qin, Cheng, and the other prefectures in surrender.

sentences.zh: 天成初，用為閬州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was employed as training commissioner of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng he was made training commissioner of Lang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召還為左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to be great general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as great general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 常以奸佞揣人主意，明宗尤愛之。

translations.literal: He constantly used treachery and flattery to gauge others' intentions; Emperor Mingzong especially favored him.
translations.idiomatic: He was forever scheming and flattering to read men's minds, and Mingzong favored him above others.

sentences.zh: 長興末，明宗謂侍臣曰：「安重霸朕之故人，以秦州歸國，其功不細，酬以團練防禦，恐非懷來之道。

translations.literal: Late in Changxing, Emperor Mingzong said to his attendants: "An Zhongba is an old acquaintance of mine. In surrendering Qinzhou to the state his merit was no small matter; to reward him with only a training or defense commission may not be the way to draw men in.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Changxing Mingzong told his attendants, "An Zhongba is an old friend. His surrender of Qinzhou was no small service; to reward him with only a training or defense post may not be the way to win men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 」範延光曰：「將校內有自河東、河北從陛下龍飛故人，尚有未及團防者，今若遽授重霸方鎮，恐為人竊議。

translations.literal: " Fan Yanguang said: "Among the officers there are old companions from Hedong and Hebei who followed Your Majesty when the dragon flew and who have still not reached even training or defense posts; if we now hastily grant Zhongba a frontier commission, I fear men will whisper in private.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Yanguang said, "Among the commanders are old companions from Hedong and Hebei who followed Your Majesty from the beginning and have not yet received even training or defense commands; to give Zhongba a circuit commission at once may invite whispered complaint.

sentences.zh: 」明宗不悅。

translations.literal: " Emperor Mingzong was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong was displeased.

sentences.zh: 未幾，竟以同州節鉞授之。

translations.literal: Before long he was after all granted the commander's baton and axe of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he received the Tongzhou commission anyway.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，移授西京留守、京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was transferred and appointed Western Capital regent and metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai he was made regent of the Western Capital and metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 先是，秦、雍之間，令長設酒食，私丐於部民者，俗謂之「搗蒜」。

translations.literal: Earlier, between Qin and Yong, when magistrates and elders set out food and drink and privately begged from the people of their districts, the custom called it "pounding garlic."
translations.idiomatic: Previously in Qin and Yong, when local officials held feasts and privately extorted from their subjects, the people called it "pounding garlic."

sentences.zh: 及重霸之鎮長安，亦為之，故秦人目重霸為「搗蒜老」。

translations.literal: When Zhongba took up his post at Chang'an he did the same, so the people of Qin called Zhongba "Old Pound-Garlic."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongba governed Chang'an he did likewise, and the Qin people nicknamed him "Old Pound-Garlic."

sentences.zh: 其年冬，改雲州節度。

translations.literal: That winter he was changed to military commissioner of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was transferred to commissioner of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 居無何，以病求代，時家寄上黨，及歸而卒。

translations.literal: After a short stay he requested replacement because of illness; his family was then lodged at Shangdang, and he died on returning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked to be relieved on account of illness; his family was at Shangdang, and he died on the way home.

sentences.zh: 重霸善悅人，好賂遺，時人目之為俊。

translations.literal: Zhongba was skilled at pleasing others and fond of giving bribes and gifts; men of the time regarded him as clever.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongba knew how to please people and loved to hand out gifts; contemporaries considered him a clever operator.

sentences.zh: 弟重進，尤凶惡。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chongjin was especially fierce and vicious.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chongjin was even more brutal.

sentences.zh: 事莊宗，以試劍殺人，奔淮南。

translations.literal: He served Emperor Zhuangzong; while testing his sword he killed a man and fled to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He served Zhuangzong, killed a man while trying out his sword, and fled to Huainan.

sentences.zh: （《玉堂閑話》：安重進，性凶險，莊宗潛龍時為小校，常佩劍列於翊衛。

translations.literal: (The 《Yutang Xianhua》 says: An Chongjin was by nature fierce and dangerous. When Emperor Zhuangzong was still a hidden dragon he was a junior officer, always wearing a sword and standing in the imperial guard.)
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Yutang Xianhua》: An Chongjin was violent by nature. While Zhuangzong was still heir apparent he served as a junior officer in the imperial guard, sword at his side.)

sentences.zh: 後攜劍南馳，投於梁祖，梁祖壯之，俾隸淮之鎮戍。

translations.literal: Later he took his sword and galloped south, throwing himself on the Liang Founder, who admired his spirit and had him attached to the Huai garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He later rode south with his sword, joined the Liang founder, who admired his spirit and assigned him to the Huai frontier garrison.

sentences.zh: 復以射殺掌庾吏，逃竄江湖，淮帥得之，擢為裨將。）〉

translations.literal: Again he shot and killed a granary officer, fled and wandered the rivers and lakes; the Huai commander got hold of him and promoted him to adjutant.) ]
translations.idiomatic: He later shot dead a granary officer, fled into the countryside, and was taken up by the Huai commander as an adjutant.)]

sentences.zh: 重霸在蜀，聞之蜀主，取之於吳，用為裨將。

translations.literal: Zhongba was in Shu; he informed the Shu ruler, who took him from Wu and employed him as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongba was in Shu he told the Shu emperor, who obtained Chongjin from Wu and made him an adjutant.

sentences.zh: 隨重霸為龍武小將，戍長道，又殺人，奔歸洛陽。

translations.literal: He followed Zhongba as a junior officer of the Dragon Martial army, garrisoned at Changdao, killed another man, and fled back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhongba as a Dragon Martial junior officer at Changdao, killed again, and fled back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: （《玉堂閑話》云：蜀破，重進東歸，明宗補為諸州馬步軍都指揮使，後有過，鞭背卒。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Yutang Xianhua》 says: When Shu fell, Chongjin returned east; Emperor Mingzong appointed him commander of the horse and foot armies of the various prefectures. Later he committed an offense and was flogged on the back until he died.) ]
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Yutang Xianhua》: After Shu fell Chongjin returned east; Mingzong made him commander of the combined horse and foot forces of the prefectures. He later offended and was flogged to death.)]

sentences.zh: 重霸之子曰懷浦，晉天福中，為禁軍指揮使。

translations.literal: Zhongba's son was named Huaipu; in the Tianfu era of Jin he was commander of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongba's son Huaipu served in the Jin Tianfu era as a palace guard commander.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇澶州，以臨陣忸怩，為景延廣所誅。

translations.literal: When the Khitan raided Chunzhou he showed bashfulness before the battle line and was executed by Jing Yanguang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan attacked Chunzhou he shrank from the fight and was executed by Jing Yanguang.

sentences.zh: 劉訓，字遵範，隰州永和人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xun, style Zunfan, was a native of Yonghe in Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun, whose style was Zunfan, came from Yonghe in Xi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 出身行間，初事武皇為馬軍隊長，漸至散將。

translations.literal: He rose from the ranks; at first he served the Martial Emperor as captain of the horse army and gradually reached the post of irregular general.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks, first serving the Martial Emperor as a cavalry captain and eventually becoming a field general.

sentences.zh: 屬河中王氏昆仲有尋戈之役，訓從史儼攻陝州。

translations.literal: When the Wang brothers of Hezhong had their fraternal strife, Xun followed Shi Yan in attacking Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the civil war among the Wang brothers of Hezhong, Xun followed Shi Yan in the attack on Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 武皇討王行瑜，以訓為前鋒，後隸河中，為隰州防禦都將。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor campaigned against Wang Xingyu and made Xun vanguard; later he was attached to Hezhong as defense commander of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Martial Emperor campaigned against Wang Xingyu, Xun led the van; he later entered Hezhong service as defense commander of Xi.

sentences.zh: 居無何，殺陝州刺史，以郡歸莊宗，曆瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: After a short time he killed the prefect of Shanzhou, surrendered the commandery to Emperor Zhuangzong, and served in turn as prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he killed the prefect of Shan, surrendered the commandery to Zhuangzong, and later served as prefect of Ying.

sentences.zh: 同光初，拜左監衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was appointed great general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang he was made great general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 三年，授襄州節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed military commissioner of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made commissioner of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，洛陽有變，訓以私忿害節度副使胡裝，族其家，聞者冤之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year there was turmoil in Luoyang; Xun, from private resentment, harmed the deputy military commissioner Hu Zhuang and exterminated his clan; those who heard of it considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year, when Luoyang was in turmoil, Xun killed his deputy Hu Zhuang in a private grudge and wiped out Hu's family—a deed widely judged unjust.

sentences.zh: 天成中，荊南高季興叛，詔訓為南面行營招討使，知荊南行府事。

translations.literal: In Tiancheng, when Jingnan's Gao Jixing rebelled, Xun was ordered to be southern campaign pacification commissioner and to manage the Jingnan field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng, when Gao Jixing of Jingnan rebelled, Xun was appointed southern campaign commander with authority over the Jingnan field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 是時，湖南馬殷請以舟師會，及王師至荊渚，殷軍方到岳州。

translations.literal: At that time Hunan's Ma Yin offered to join with a fleet; when the royal army reached Jingzhu, Yin's army had only just arrived at Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin of Hunan had offered a naval contingent, but when the imperial army reached Jingzhou his fleet had only just reached Yue.

sentences.zh: 仍傳意於訓，許助軍儲弓甲之類，久之，略無至者。

translations.literal: He still sent word to Xun promising aid in military stores, bows, armor, and the like, but after a long time virtually nothing arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Yin still sent assurances of grain, arms, and armor, yet after a long wait almost nothing came.

sentences.zh: （案《通鑒》：劉訓至荊南，楚王殷遣都指揮使許德勳等將水軍屯岳州。

translations.literal: (According to the 《Zizhi Tongjian》: When Liu Xun reached Jingnan, King Yin of Chu sent Commander-in-Chief Xu Dexun and others to lead the water army and encamp at Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: (Per the 《Zizhi Tongjian》: When Liu Xun reached Jingnan, King Yin of Chu sent Xu Dexun and others with the fleet to encamp at Yue.

sentences.zh: 高季興堅壁不戰，求救於吳，吳人遣水軍援之。）〉

translations.literal: Gao Jixing held his walls and would not fight, begged aid from Wu, and the Wu sent a water army to reinforce him.) ]
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jixing held his walls and refused battle, begged Wu for help, and Wu sent naval reinforcements.)]

sentences.zh: 荊渚地氣卑濕，漸及霖潦，糧運不繼，人多疾疫。

translations.literal: The Jingzhu region's air was low and damp; gradually heavy rains and floods came, grain transport could not keep up, and many men fell to pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingzhou lowlands were humid; rains and floods followed, supplies failed, and pestilence spread through the army.

sentences.zh: 訓本無將略，人鹹苦之。

translations.literal: Xun by nature had no military strategy, and all men suffered under him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had no talent for command, and the troops suffered under him.

sentences.zh: 及孔循至，得襄之小校獻竹龍之術，及造竹龍二道，傅於城下，竟無所濟。

translations.literal: When Kong Xun arrived, he obtained a junior officer of Xiang who presented the technique of bamboo dragons; they built two bamboo dragons and placed them against the walls, but in the end it availed nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Xun came, a junior officer from Xiang offered a "bamboo dragon" siege device; they built two and set them against the walls, but they accomplished nothing.

sentences.zh: 遂罷兵，令將士散略居民而回。

translations.literal: They then dismissed the army and ordered officers and soldiers to scatter and plunder the inhabitants on the way back.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew the army and let the troops plunder the countryside on the march home.

sentences.zh: 詔訓赴闕，尋責授檀州刺史，續敕濮州安置，未幾，起為龍武大將軍，尋授建雄軍節度使，移鎮延平。

translations.literal: Xun was ordered to the capital; soon he was demoted and appointed prefect of Tanzhou, then further ordered settled at Puzhou. Before long he was raised to great general of the Dragon Martial guard, then appointed military commissioner of the Jianxiong army and transferred to garrison Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was recalled to court, demoted to prefect of Tan, then confined at Pu; soon he was restored as Dragon Martial great general, made commissioner of Jianxiong, and transferred to Yanping.

sentences.zh: 卒贈太尉。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 劉彥琮，字比德，雲中人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yancong, style Bide, was a native of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yancong, whose style was Bide, came from Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 事武皇，累從征役。

translations.literal: He served the Martial Emperor and repeatedly followed campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Martial Emperor through many campaigns.

sentences.zh: 先是，絳州刺史王瓘叛，武皇言於彥琮，意欲致之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the prefect of Jiangzhou Wang Jin had rebelled; the Martial Emperor spoke to Yancong, intending to bring him in.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Jiang prefect Wang Jin had rebelled; the Martial Emperor told Yancong he wanted Jin brought in.

sentences.zh: 無幾，從略於汾、晉之郊，彥琮奔絳，瓘以為附己，待之甚厚，因命為騎將。

translations.literal: Before long, on a foray in the suburbs of Fen and Jin, Yancong fled to Jiang; Jin thought he had attached himself and treated him very generously, appointing him cavalry officer.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on a raid near Fen and Jin, Yancong defected to Jiang; Jin thought he had come over willingly, treated him generously, and made him a cavalry officer.

sentences.zh: 會瓘出獵，於馳驅之際，彥琮刃瓘之首來獻，武皇甚奇之。

translations.literal: When Jin went out hunting, in the midst of the gallop Yancong cut off Jin's head and came to present it; the Martial Emperor marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin went hunting, Yancong struck off his head in mid-gallop and presented it to the Martial Emperor, who was astonished.

sentences.zh: 從莊宗解上黨之圍。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Zhuangzong in relieving the siege of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhuangzong in relieving the siege of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 同光初，稍遷至鐵林指揮使、磁州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was gradually promoted to commander of the Iron Forest guard and prefect of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang he rose to commander of the Iron Forest guard and prefect of Ci.

sentences.zh: 後明宗赴難京師，授華州留後，尋正授節旄。

translations.literal: Later, when Emperor Mingzong went to the capital's aid, he was appointed regent of Huazhou and soon formally granted the commander's insignia.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong marched to save the capital, Yancong was made regent of Hua and soon received a full commission.

sentences.zh: 天成三年，改左武衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng he was changed to senior general of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng 3 he was made senior general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改陝州節度使，尋移鎮邠州，卒於鎮，時年六十四。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to military commissioner of Shanzhou, then transferred to garrison Binzhou; he died in his commission at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made commissioner of Shan, then transferred to Bin, where he died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 袁建豐，武皇破巢時得於華陰，年方九歲，愛其精神爽俊，俾收養之。

translations.literal: Yuan Jianfeng was obtained at Huayin when the Martial Emperor defeated Huang Chao; he was only nine years old, and because his spirit was bright and handsome he was taken in and reared.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jianfeng was taken at Huayin when the Martial Emperor defeated Huang Chao; he was only nine, and his bright bearing led the emperor to adopt him.

sentences.zh: 漸長，列於左右，復習騎射，補鐵林都虞候。

translations.literal: As he grew he was placed at the ruler's side, again studied riding and archery, and was appointed deputy commander of the Iron Forest guard.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he served at court, trained in horsemanship and archery, and became deputy commander of the Iron Forest guard.

sentences.zh: 從破邠州王行瑜，以功遷左親騎軍使，轉突騎指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed in the defeat of Wang Xingyu of Binzhou and, for merit, was promoted to commander of the Left Personal Cavalry and then commander of the shock cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in the defeat of Wang Xingyu of Bin and was promoted to commander of the Left Personal Cavalry, then of the shock cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從莊宗解圍上黨，破柏鄉陣，累功遷右僕射、左廂馬軍指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Zhuangzong in relieving the siege of Shangdang, broke the formation at Baixiang, and through repeated merit was promoted to Right Vice Director and commander of the left wing of the horse army.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved Shangdang with Zhuangzong, broke the enemy at Baixiang, and rose through merit to Right Vice Director and commander of the left cavalry wing.

sentences.zh: 明宗為內衙指揮使，建豐為副。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was commander of the inner palace guard, Jianfeng was his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong commanded the inner guard, Jianfeng served as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 北討劉守光，常身先士伍，轉都教練使，權蕃漢副總管。

translations.literal: In the northern campaign against Liu Shouguang he constantly led the ranks in person; he was transferred to chief training officer and acting deputy overseer of the frontier and Chinese forces.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning north against Liu Shouguang he often led from the front; he became chief training officer and acting deputy overseer of the combined frontier forces.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入鄴，以心腹幹能，選為魏府都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Ye, because he was a trusted man of ability he was chosen as chief inspector of the Wei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong entered Ye he chose Jianfeng, a trusted and capable man, as chief inspector of the Wei prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從征劉鄩，下衛、磁、洺有功，加檢校司空，授州洺州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Liu Kun, took Wei, Ci, and Ming with merit, was added acting Minister of Works, and appointed prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Liu Kun he captured Wei, Ci, and Ming, was made acting Minister of Works, and appointed prefect of Ming.

sentences.zh: 於臨洺西敗梁將王遷數千人，生獲將領七十餘人，俄拜相州刺史。

translations.literal: West of Linming he defeated several thousand men under the Liang general Wang Qian and captured more than seventy officers alive; soon he was appointed prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: West of Linming he routed several thousand men under the Liang general Wang Qian and took more than seventy officers alive; he was soon made prefect of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 征赴河上，豫戰於胡柳陂。

translations.literal: On campaign to the Yellow River he fought beforehand at Huliu Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Marching to the Yellow River front he fought at Huliu Ford.

sentences.zh: 建豐領相州軍士，行營在外，委州事於小人，失於撫馭，指揮使孟守謙據城以叛，建豐引兵討平之。

translations.literal: Jianfeng led the Xiangzhou troops with his field camp abroad; he entrusted prefectural affairs to petty men and failed in governing and control, so Commander Meng Shouqian seized the city in rebellion; Jianfeng led troops to suppress and pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: With his army in the field Jianfeng left Xiang in the hands of unworthy subordinates; Commander Meng Shouqian rebelled and seized the city, and Jianfeng returned to crush him.

sentences.zh: 改隰州刺史，染風痹於任。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Xizhou and contracted wind paralysis in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xi prefecture and contracted paralysis while in office.

sentences.zh: 明宗嗣位，念及平昔副貳之舊，詔赴洛下，親幸其第，撫問隆厚，加檢校太傅，遙授鎮南節度使，俾請俸自給。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong succeeded, remembering their old ties as chief and deputy, he ordered him to Luoyang, personally visited his residence with generous consolation, added acting Grand Tutor, and remotely appointed him military commissioner of Zhennan, allowing him to draw salary for his own support.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong succeeded he recalled their old partnership, summoned Jianfeng to Luoyang, visited his home with warm condolences, made him acting Grand Tutor and titular commissioner of Zhennan, and allowed him to draw a salary for his upkeep.

sentences.zh: 後卒於洛陽，年五十六。

translations.literal: Later he died at Luoyang at the age of fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in Luoyang at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 廢朝一日，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Court audiences were suspended for one day; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court for a day and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 子可鈞，仕皇朝，位至諸衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His son Kejun served the imperial dynasty and rose to great general of the various guards.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kejun served the dynasty and rose to great general of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 西方鄴，定州滿城人也。

translations.literal: Xi Fangye was a native of Mancheng in Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Fangye came from Mancheng in Ding prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父再遇，為州軍校。

translations.literal: His father Zaiyu was a garrison officer of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zaiyu was a prefectural garrison officer.

sentences.zh: 鄴居軍中，以勇力聞。

translations.literal: Fangye lived in the army and was known for courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Fangye grew up in the army and was famed for his strength.

sentences.zh: 年二十，南渡河遊梁，不見用，復歸。

translations.literal: At twenty he crossed the river south to seek service in Liang, was not employed, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he crossed south to seek service with Liang, found no post, and came home.

sentences.zh: 莊宗以為孝義軍指揮使，累從征伐皆有功。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong made him commander of the Xiaoyi army; he repeatedly followed campaigns and always had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong made him commander of the Xiaoyi army, and he distinguished himself in campaign after campaign.

sentences.zh: 同光中，為曹州刺史，以州兵屯汴州。

translations.literal: In Tongguang he was prefect of Caozhou and stationed the prefectural troops at Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Tongguang he was prefect of Cao and posted his troops at Bian.

sentences.zh: 明宗自魏州，南渡河，時莊宗東幸汴州。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong came from Weizhou and crossed the river south; at the time Emperor Zhuangzong was traveling east to Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong marched south from Wei while Zhuangzong was traveling east to Bian.

sentences.zh: 汴州節度使孔循懷二誌，使北門迎明宗，西門迎莊宗，所以供帳委積悉如一，曰：「先至者入之。

translations.literal: The Bianzhou military commissioner Kong Xun harbored two intentions, had the north gate receive Mingzong and the west gate receive Zhuangzong, and made all supplies and stores identical, saying: "Whoever arrives first may enter.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian commissioner Kong Xun hedged his bets, prepared the north gate for Mingzong and the west gate for Zhuangzong, stocked both equally, and said, "Whoever arrives first may enter.

sentences.zh: 」 鄴因責循曰：「主上破梁室於公，有不殺之恩，奈何欲納總管而負國？

translations.literal: " Fangye therefore rebuked Xun: "Our lord destroyed the Liang house for you and showed the grace of not killing you—how can you wish to welcome the chief commander and betray the state?
translations.idiomatic: " Fangye rebuked him: "Our lord destroyed Liang for your sake and spared your life—how can you welcome the chief commander and betray the throne?

sentences.zh: 」循不答。

translations.literal: " Xun did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Xun made no reply.

sentences.zh: 鄴度循不可爭，以石敬瑭妻，明宗女也，時方在汴，欲殺之以堅人心。

translations.literal: Fangye judged that Xun could not be argued with; Shi Jingtang's wife, who was Emperor Mingzong's daughter, was then at Bian, and he wished to kill her to steady men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Xun would not yield, Fangye considered killing Shi Jingtang's wife—the emperor's daughter, then at Bian—to steady loyalty.

sentences.zh: 循知其謀，取之藏其家，鄴無如之何。

translations.literal: Xun learned of the plot, took her and hid her in his house, and Fangye could do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Xun learned of the plan, took her into hiding, and Fangye was helpless.

sentences.zh: 而明宗已及汴，乃將麾下兵五百騎西迎莊宗，見於汜水，嗚咽泣下，莊宗亦為之噓唏，使以兵為先鋒。

translations.literal: But Mingzong had already reached Bian; Fangye then led five hundred horsemen of his command west to welcome Zhuangzong, met him at Sishui, sobbed and wept, and Zhuangzong also sighed for him and had his troops serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong had already reached Bian; Fangye led five hundred horsemen west to meet Zhuangzong at Sishui, wept before him, and Zhuangzong, moved in turn, made his men the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 莊宗至汴西，不得入，還洛陽，遇弑。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong reached the west of Bian but could not enter, returned to Luoyang, and met assassination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong reached the west bank of Bian but could not enter, returned to Luoyang, and was murdered.

sentences.zh: 明宗入洛，鄴請死於馬前，明宗嘉歎久之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong entered Luoyang, Fangye asked to die before his horse; Mingzong praised and sighed over him for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong entered Luoyang, Fangye asked to die at his horse's feet; Mingzong praised him at length.

sentences.zh: 明年，荊南高季興叛，明宗遣襄州節度使劉訓等招討，而以東川董璋為西南招討使，乃拜鄴夔州刺史，副璋，以兵出三峽。

translations.literal: The next year, when Jingnan's Gao Jixing rebelled, Mingzong sent the Xiang military commissioner Liu Xun and others to pacify him, and made Dongchuan's Dong Zhang southwestern pacification commissioner; Fangye was appointed prefect of Qizhou to assist Zhang and led troops out through the Three Gorges.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Gao Jixing of Jingnan rebelled, Mingzong sent Liu Xun of Xiang and others against him and made Dong Zhang of Dongchuan southwestern commander; Fangye was made prefect of Qi to assist Zhang and marched through the Three Gorges.

sentences.zh: 已而訓等無功見黜，諸將皆罷，璋未嘗出兵，惟鄴獨取夔、忠、萬三州，乃以夔州為寧江軍，拜鄴節度使。

translations.literal: Before long Xun and the others were dismissed without merit; all the generals were relieved, and Zhang never once sent out troops—only Fangye alone took Qi, Zhong, and Wan, whereupon Qi was made the Ningjiang army and Fangye was appointed military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xun and the others were dismissed for failure; the other generals were recalled and Zhang never marched—only Fangye captured Qi, Zhong, and Wan, after which Qi was organized as the Ningjiang circuit and Fangye was made its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 已而又取歸州，數敗季興之兵。

translations.literal: Before long he also took Guizhou and repeatedly defeated Jixing's troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Gui as well and repeatedly defeated Jixing's forces.

sentences.zh: 鄴，武人，所為多不中法度，判官譚善達數以諫鄴，鄴怒，遣人告善達受人金，下獄。

translations.literal: Fangye was a military man whose actions mostly failed to accord with law; his aide Tan Shanda repeatedly remonstrated with him. Fangye was angry, sent men to accuse Shanda of taking bribes, and put him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier by trade, Fangye often ignored the law; his aide Tan Shanda remonstrated repeatedly until Fangye, enraged, had him accused of bribery and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 善達素剛，辭益不遜，遂死於獄中。

translations.literal: Shanda was by nature stubborn; his words grew ever more insubordinate, and he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Shanda was stubborn by nature and grew only more defiant in speech until he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 鄴病，見善達為祟，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: Fangye fell ill, saw Shanda as a haunting spirit, and died in his commission.
translations.idiomatic: Fangye fell ill, was haunted by visions of Shanda, and died at his post.

sentences.zh: 孫璋，齊州曆城人。

translations.literal: Sun Zhang was a native of Licheng in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhang came from Licheng in Qi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 出身行間，隸梁將楊師厚麾下，稍補奉化軍使。

translations.literal: He rose from the ranks, was attached to the Liang general Yang Shihou, and was gradually appointed commander of the Fenghua army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks under the Liang general Yang Shihou and was eventually made commander of the Fenghua garrison.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入鄴，累遷澶州都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Ye he was repeatedly promoted to commander of Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong entered Ye, Zhang rose to commander of Chun.

sentences.zh: 明宗鎮常山，擢為裨校。

translations.literal: When Mingzong held Changshan he was promoted to adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong governed Changshan, Zhang was promoted to adjutant.

sentences.zh: 鄴兵之變，從明宗赴難京師。

translations.literal: At the mutiny of the Ye troops he followed Mingzong to the capital's aid.
translations.idiomatic: During the Ye mutiny he followed Mingzong to save the capital.

sentences.zh: 天成初，曆趙、登二州刺史，齊州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he served in turn as prefect of Zhao and Deng and as defense commissioner of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng he served as prefect of Zhao and Deng in turn, then as defense commissioner of Qi.

sentences.zh: 王都之據中山，璋為定州行營都虞候，賊平，加檢校太保。

translations.literal: When Wang Du held Zhongshan, Zhang was chief adjutant of the Dingzhou field camp; when the bandit was pacified he was added acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Du held Zhongshan, Zhang was chief adjutant of the Ding field camp; after the rebellion was crushed he was made acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 長興初，授鄜州節度使，罷鎮，卒於洛陽，年六十一。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changxing he was appointed military commissioner of Fuzhou; relieved of his commission, he died at Luoyang at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Changxing he was made commissioner of Fu; after leaving his post he died in Luoyang at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫天地斯晦，則帝王於是龍飛；

translations.literal: The historian says: When Heaven and Earth are thus darkened, emperors and kings then rise like dragons;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When heaven and earth fall into darkness, emperors rise like dragons.

sentences.zh: 雲雷構屯，則王侯以之蟬蛻。

translations.literal: when clouds and thunder gather in the hexagram Tun, kings and marquises thereby cast off their shells.
translations.idiomatic: When cloud and thunder gather as in the hexagram Tun, lords cast off their old forms.

sentences.zh: 良以適遭亂世，得奮雄圖，故金全而下，咸以軍旅之功，坐登藩閫之位，垂名簡冊，亦可貴焉。

translations.literal: Truly because they happened to meet a chaotic age and could exert bold designs, therefore from Jinquan downward all, through merit in military campaigns, sat and ascended to frontier commissioner posts, leaving their names on the bamboo slips—this too is estimable.
translations.idiomatic: Having come of age in turmoil and seized their chance to prove themselves, Jinquan and the men below him won frontier commands through military service and a place in the annals—an achievement worth honoring.

sentences.zh: 惟重霸以奸險而仗旄鉞，蓋非數子之儔也。

translations.literal: Only Zhongba, through treachery and danger, bore the commander's baton and axe—he was surely not the equal of these several men.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhongba, cunning and treacherous, won a commander's commission—he was hardly the equal of the others.
